_about: Six findings from the first real three-lens run (2026-10-08) against a per-item-discount diff with one planted bug: discount applied to the first unit only. Expected: 3 unique — the planted bug, the missing 0..100 check, the qty-1 test.

findings.claim: Discount is applied only to the first unit of a line; spec requires it on every unit.
findings.failure_scenario: lineTotal({price:100, qty:3, discountPct:10}) returns 290; SPEC.md acceptance requires 270. Any line with qty>1 and a discount is overcharged.

findings.claim: discountPct is not validated against the spec range 0..100.
findings.failure_scenario: {price:100, qty:1, discountPct:150} gives -50; discountPct:-5 gives 105 (a surcharge). Negative totals flow into subtotal.

findings.claim: Discount is applied to only one unit of the line, contradicting the spec that it applies to every unit; customers are overcharged.
findings.failure_scenario: items=[{price:100,qty:3,discountPct:10}] -> lineTotal returns 290; SPEC acceptance requires 270. Existing test uses qty 1 so it does not catch it.

findings.claim: discountPct is not validated to 0..100 or numeric; a value outside range or non-number yields negative/NaN totals if any writer ever lets a user set it.
findings.failure_scenario: cart item {price:100,qty:1,discountPct:150} -> unit=-50, total negative; discountPct:'abc' -> NaN. No write path to db.carts in this repo, so reachability is unproven.

findings.claim: Discount is applied only to one unit of the line, not every unit as the spec requires.
findings.failure_scenario: lineTotal({price:100, qty:3, discountPct:10}) -> 290 instead of 270 (spec acceptance); discountPct 100 qty 3 -> 200 instead of 0.

findings.claim: The discount test uses qty 1, so it passes with the buggy implementation. The spec's acceptance example (qty 3 -> 270) is not tested.
findings.failure_scenario: Any implementation that discounts only one unit passes: npm test is green (2/2) while lineTotal({price:100,qty:3,discountPct:10}) returns 290.
